name: Caroline Shinkle
bio: Caroline Shinkle is a corporate lawyer who has worked at Cravath, Swaine & Moore on mergers, capital markets and financial regulation. She graduated from Harvard Law School in 2020, moved to New York City that year, and earlier interned at the Federal Reserve Board, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Israel. This is her first campaign for federal office.

platform.point: Eliminate federal income tax on W-2 wages and pursue a balanced budget amendment and zero-based budgeting.
Lower taxes on work, expand housing supply and pursue targeted deregulation under a 'Protect the Paycheck' agenda.
Increase support for law enforcement and first responders.
Combat antisemitism and stand with the Jewish community and Israel.
Increase competition and price transparency in health care and pass the Access to Breast Cancer Diagnosis Act.
Improve education quality and affordability through innovation.

economy.evidence: Wants to end federal income tax on wages, shrink government sharply and adopt a balanced budget amendment.

security.evidence: Makes support for law enforcement a campaign priority and would exempt Homeland Security from spending cuts.

immigration.evidence: Backs ICE enforcement against dangerous undocumented immigrants while leaving room to discuss working immigrants without rewarding lawbreaking.

foreign.evidence: Supports military operations against Iran and a peace-through-strength agenda backing allies.

notes: Security score added from her campaign's law-enforcement priority and interview remarks; evidence is limited.

name: Darializa Avila Chevalier
current_role: Sociology doctoral candidate and community organizer
bio: Darializa Avila Chevalier is a sociology doctoral candidate at the CUNY Graduate Center who has worked as an investigator at the Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem and taught at Lehman College and NYU. Born in Florida to Dominican immigrant parents, she studied at Columbia and has organized in upper Manhattan on housing, immigration and Palestine issues. She won the 2026 Democratic primary in NY-13, defeating incumbent Adriano Espaillat.

platform.point: Abolish ICE, end deportations and expand pathways to citizenship.
Pass Medicare for All to create a single-payer health system.
Fund social housing federally and strengthen tenant protections under a Housing for All plan.
Shift federal money from the military to schools, housing and social programs under 'Babies, Not Bombs'.
Supports the Block the Bombs Act to limit weapons transfers to Israel.
Ban large super PACs and bar members of Congress from trading stocks.

economy.evidence: Democratic socialist who backs worker ownership, federally funded social housing and action against corporate greed.

welfare.evidence: Supports single-payer Medicare for All and universal housing.

security.evidence: Supports prison abolition and investing in mental health and housing in place of policing.

immigration.evidence: Calls for abolishing ICE, ending all deportations and describes open borders as an ideal.

foreign.evidence: Backs the Block the Bombs Act, opposes military aid to Israel and favors diplomacy with Russia over Ukraine.

notes: The only Commons image is a frame from a YouTube interview show, so no portrait was used.

name: Manual "Jomo" Williams
bio: Manual "Jomo" Williams is the Republican nominee in New York's 13th congressional district. He has previously run for New York City Council and filed with the FEC as a presidential candidate.

platform.point: Promotes a 'Universal Capitalism' approach as an alternative to socialism.
Opposes sanctuary city policies and calls for securing borders in a humane and fair way.
Supports the SAVE Act and election integrity litigation.
Proposes contactless police traffic stops to reduce shootings of unarmed people.
Expand youth employment programs and community investment.

immigration.evidence: Opposes sanctuary city policies and backs border security while describing his approach as humane.

notes: Some listings show him as an independent and name manualwilliams.com as his site; the ballot name spelling 'Manual' is kept from the input.

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
bio: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has represented New York's 14th district since 2019 after defeating incumbent Joe Crowley in the 2018 primary. Born in the Bronx and raised in Yorktown, she studied economics and international relations at Boston University and worked as an educator and in restaurants before running. Her first bill was the Green New Deal resolution.

platform.point: Pursue a Green New Deal: a ten-year mobilization to cut pollution and create union infrastructure jobs.
Cap credit card interest rates at 15% through the Loan Shark Prevention Act.
Advance 'Just Society' bills on living wages, poverty measures and renters' rights.
Supports Medicare for All.
Supports tuition-free public colleges.

economy.evidence: Advocates higher taxes on the wealthy, worker cooperatives and a 15% credit card interest cap.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and LGBTQ rights, while backing gun safety groups such as Moms Demand Action.

immigration.evidence: Has called for abolishing ICE and educates immigrants on their legal rights.

foreign.evidence: Voted present on 2021 Iron Dome funding, against a 2025 amendment to cut it, and says she has never voted for aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Lead sponsor of the Green New Deal resolution to phase out fossil fuels.

tech.evidence: Co-led the DEFIANCE Act on non-consensual deepfakes and has opposed AI data centers over environmental harm.

education.evidence: Supports tuition-free public colleges and public education funding.

name: Diamant Hysenaj
bio: Diamant Hysenaj is a construction entrepreneur who founded DCG New York Inc. in 2014 after an earlier firm closed in the 2008 financial crisis. Born in Kosovo, he immigrated to the Bronx at age nine in 1991. He is endorsed by the Republican and Conservative parties in the Bronx and Queens.

platform.point: Draws on his construction background to build more quality housing and create local jobs.
Pairs secure borders with faster citizenship for law-abiding immigrants.
Support small businesses and create jobs in the district.
Lower costs by cutting inefficiency and fraud in the health system.
Make streets safe enough for children to play outside.

economy.evidence: Supports cutting taxes, shrinking government and reducing regulation for businesses.

immigration.evidence: Calls for secure borders combined with faster citizenship for law-abiding immigrants.

name: Ritchie Torres
bio: Ritchie Torres has represented New York's 15th district since 2021. Raised in public housing in the Bronx, he served on the New York City Council from 2014 to 2020, where he chaired the public housing and oversight committees. He won the 2026 Democratic primary over Michael Blake and Jose Vega.

platform.point: Make rent affordable for Bronx families.
Keep children safe on their way to school; says the defund-police movement is over.
Supports Israel as a self-described pro-Israel progressive and opposed early Gaza ceasefire calls.
Supports the Green New Deal and addressing environmental harm from the Cross Bronx Expressway.
Help working families cover their basic costs.

security.evidence: Reversed earlier support for defunding police, declaring the movement dead in 2022.

immigration.evidence: Cosponsored the New Way Forward Act but voted for the Laken Riley Act in 2025.

foreign.evidence: Voted for the April 2024 Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan aid packages.

energy.evidence: Supports the Green New Deal and was endorsed by the League of Conservation Voters.

tech.evidence: Member of the Congressional Blockchain Caucus who criticized SEC crypto enforcement and urged regulators to allow election betting markets.

name: Stylo Sapaskis
bio: Stylo A. Sapaskis is a Bronx Republican who was his party's nominee in NY-15 in 2022. He has also run for the New York State Senate in 2010 and New York City Council District 11 in 2025.

platform.point: Criticized inflation and high gas and food prices.
Has backed a $20 minimum wage and more aid for higher education.
Supports ending government funding for abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood.
Supports a larger police presence.

notes: Platform points come from voter-guide answers summarized by City & State and may date from his 2022 campaign; too thin to score.

name: Gonzalo Duran
current_role: Vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party
bio: Gonzalo Duran is a military veteran and founder of Devil Dog USA, which helps veterans move into civilian life. He is vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party and a district leader for the 79th Assembly District, having left the Democratic Party in 2023. He previously ran for Congress in NY-15 in 2024.

platform.point: Restore accountability, personal responsibility and economic opportunity in the Bronx, and oppose socialism.
Support veterans, including those affected by burn pit exposure.
Lists public safety among his core campaign issues.
Lists housing, employment and transportation as campaign priorities for the Bronx.

notes: His campaign site lists issue areas without detailed positions, so no domains are scored.

name: Andre Easton
bio: Andre Easton is a lifelong Bronx resident who has taught high school English in South Bronx public schools since 2012. He is a member of the Party for Socialism and Liberation and is running as an independent with an all-volunteer campaign.

platform.point: Cap rent at 20% of household income and repeal the Faircloth Amendment to build new public housing.
Raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour and create a federal jobs guarantee with union wages.
Create a single-payer health system with free mental health and maternal care.
Make childcare, pre-K and public college free, cancel student debt and equalize school funding.
End US military aid to Israel and impose an arms embargo.
Raise taxes on the ultra-wealthy and cut the military budget by 90%.

economy.evidence: Proposes a $30 minimum wage, a federal jobs guarantee, higher taxes on billionaires and public grocery chains.

welfare.evidence: Calls for single-payer health care and free childcare and pre-K.

liberty.evidence: On abortion he would enshrine and fully fund access; on LGBTQ rights he backs anti-discrimination protections; on drugs he favors treatment over policing.

security.evidence: Would end mass incarceration, end police militarization through the 1033 program and fund violence interruption instead.

immigration.evidence: Calls for full legal status for undocumented immigrants.

foreign.evidence: Would cut the military budget by 90% and end military aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Proposes replacing diesel trucks with zero-emission fleets and electrifying school buses as part of climate justice.

education.evidence: Calls for equal public school funding, tuition-free college and free community-run pre-K.

name: George Latimer
bio: George Latimer, a Mount Vernon native, has represented New York's 16th district since January 2025. He previously served as Westchester County Executive from 2018 to 2025, in the New York State Senate and Assembly, on the Westchester County Board of Legislators and on the Rye City Council.

platform.point: Supports the Women's Health Protection Act and opposes a national abortion ban.
Backs an assault weapons ban and universal background checks.
Support Ukraine, Israel and NATO and counter China's military expansion.
Invest in renewable energy and support the Green New Deal.
Speed up work permits, create a path to citizenship and add immigration courts.
Oppose privatizing Medicare and Social Security and expand their benefits.

welfare.evidence: Wants to expand Medicare and Social Security benefits and prioritize affordable childcare.

liberty.evidence: On abortion he backs access rights and on LGBTQ issues he banned conversion therapy in Westchester, while on guns he backs an assault weapons ban.

security.evidence: As county executive he signed a law limiting county cooperation with federal immigration investigations.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to citizenship and faster work permits, and accepted asylum seekers in Westchester in 2023.

foreign.evidence: Supports aid to Ukraine and Israel and a strong NATO.

energy.evidence: Supports the Green New Deal and renewable energy investment.

education.evidence: Lists school funding as a priority for children.

notes: The security score rests on limited county-level evidence.

name: Joseph Cinquemani
bio: Joseph Cinquemani is an attorney in New Rochelle who runs his own law office serving corporate and individual clients. This is his first campaign for public office.

platform.point: Cut federal spending by 10% across the board and use savings for tax relief.
Exempt income up to the poverty line from federal income tax.
Turn Indian Point into a small modular reactor hub and expand Marcellus Shale gas drilling.
Reduce the Federal Reserve to an advisory role and let markets set interest rates.
Promote union apprenticeships and vocational training as alternatives to college.
Back Middle East alliances and military action against hostile regimes while avoiding nation-building.

economy.evidence: Proposes a 10% federal spending cut, tax relief and market-set interest rates.

foreign.evidence: Supports military action against Iran and hostile regimes and Gulf alliances, but opposes nation-building.

energy.evidence: Backs expanded natural gas drilling and new nuclear reactors to lower energy costs.

notes: The campaign site also lists Instagram, YouTube and TikTok handles, but their exact URLs were not confirmed.

name: Mike Lawler
bio: Mike Lawler, a Suffern native, has represented New York's 17th district since 2023 and chairs the House Foreign Affairs Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee. He previously served in the New York State Assembly, as deputy town supervisor of Orangetown and as executive director of the state Republican Party. He holds accounting and finance degrees from Manhattan College.

platform.point: Pushed to raise the SALT deduction cap to $40,000 and backs broader tax relief for families and seniors.
Reopen Indian Point, pursue an all-of-the-above energy strategy and oppose state CLCPA mandates.
Extend ACA subsidies and create an IVF tax credit.
Fund first responders and repeal New York's cashless bail law.
Pair border security and opposition to sanctuary policies with bipartisan reform such as the Dignity Act.
Support Ukraine, Israel and Indo-Pacific alliances.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act and backs tax cuts and a 1% cap on spending growth.

welfare.evidence: Supports stronger work requirements but crossed party lines to extend ACA subsidies.

liberty.evidence: On abortion he opposes a federal ban but backs limits; he supports same-sex marriage; on guns he backs red flag laws with due process.

security.evidence: Seeks more federal funding for police and repeal of cashless bail.

immigration.evidence: Opposes sanctuary policies but cosponsored the Dignity Act and voted to extend TPS for Haitians.

foreign.evidence: Strongly supports Ukraine and Israel and introduced an Indo-Pacific Treaty Alliance Act.

energy.evidence: Backs all-of-the-above energy and nuclear power and opposes state climate mandates, while belonging to the Climate Solutions Caucus.

education.evidence: Opposes cuts to school funding while supporting parental choice.

notes: Economy, welfare, security, energy and education scores were newly added from his campaign issues page.
